analyst_view.overall: Braga (17th, 4 pts) host KuPS (33rd, 1 pt) and need the win to push toward the top eight. Under Franclim Carvalho, who took over in October, Braga have not conceded in four games and are unbeaten in five at home; he has ruled out rotation, said he wants the game settled early, and Jonas Wind is available again. Sikou Niakate is out and counted, one report has midfielder Vitor Carvalho injured, and Gabriel Silva is a doubt. KuPS have not won in five, have scored three goals in that run, have not played a competitive game since 8 November now that the Finnish season is over, and lost winger Bob Nii Armah (counted). Ukrainian referee Oleksiy Derevinskyi is confirmed, and the numbers already trim cards a little for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, about 2.1 of them Braga's. I lean a little higher: KuPS arrive without a competitive game since 8 November and without a win in five, which the numbers can't see, and Franclim is fielding his strongest side with Wind back; a mild +4% gives about 2.7 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, about 7 for Braga, already lifted 9% for Braga's recent corner count and cut for KuPS' few. Franclim wants quick, vertical attacks rather than long spells of pressure, and KuPS will mostly defend deep, which the split already reflects, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already trimmed for both sides' quiet recent discipline and for referee Derevinskyi's low card count (-3%). A one-sided game against a team defending deep usually stays calm, which is what the numbers show, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already pushed up 26% for Braga's recent shot volume and down 13% for KuPS'. Franclim ruled out rotation and wants his side to reach the box fast and often, against a KuPS team short of match rhythm, so I lean slightly higher: +3% gives about 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, 7.6 of them Braga's. A KuPS side out of season should give up cleaner chances than usual, which the numbers can't see, and Braga field their first-choice attack with Horta and Pau Victor, so I lean slightly higher: +3% gives about 10.4.
